chunks: Sa'd narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Nu'man al-Razi, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'One call to prayer (iqamah) suffices for you in place of the second call during travel.'

key_terms.السَّفَرِ: Travel, a state that modifies certain ritual obligations.
key_terms.الْإِقَامَةِ: The call to prayer made immediately before starting the salat, distinct from the adhan.
key_terms.طَاقٌ: A single unit or one; here referring to one iqamah.

ai.seo_question: How many iqamah calls are required for prayers during travel in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Ja'far al-Sadiq to clarify the concession (*rukhsa*) granted to travelers, establishing that a single *iqamah* suffices for consecutive prayers like Dhuhr and Asr during a journey. This ruling alleviates the burden of repeated calls to prayer, reflecting the practical flexibility inherent in Shia jurisprudence for those in transit.
